description:
Summary

GrayMatter Robotics is a well-capitalized Physical AI company headquartered in Los Angeles, building Factory SuperIntelligence (FSI) through systems that learn, adapt, and develop genuine process intelligence across every part they touch. Our robots take on the tedious, hazardous, and ergonomically demanding work that has kept manufacturing dependent on a shrinking skilled workforce, delivering superhuman performance. Robotics has a demo problem. GMR doesn't. Our systems are in active production today, adapting autonomously to real geometries, real materials, and real process variation without reprogramming. We deliver our system through a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that converts capital expenditure into an operating subscription, making Physical AI accessible to the manufacturers who need it most. We hire people who want to solve hard physical problems at an industrial scale.



Role at a Glance

Forward Deployed Engineers at GMR build our business inside one customer at a time. You go to the customer's floor, take an ambiguous problem and define it clearly, then design, build and prove a solution that moves the customer's numbers. You own the result from the first conversation through operator adoption, and you carry what you learn back into the platform so the next customer benefits. Time to value matters, so you ship a working first version quickly and improve it with the people who use it.



What You Will Do

 - Get to the root of the problem. You'll work directly with customers, operators, and engineers to understand what's actually happening on the factory floor, challenge initial assumptions, and define the problems worth solving.

 - Take solutions across the finish line. You'll connect the dots across software, hardware, and manufacturing, make practical decisions, and drive execution until your work translates into meaningful results for the customer.

 - Turn local solutions into broader capabilities. You'll build features tailored to individual customer environments using GMR's platform infrastructure, while identifying opportunities to contribute those solutions back to the generalized platform.

 - Expand your reach through collaboration. You'll know when to bring in subject matter experts, leverage internal teams, and look beyond engineering to find the right solution. Success means understanding the bigger picture, from supply chain considerations to customer relationships.

 - Stay curious and keep building. No two problems are exactly alike. You'll continuously develop new skills, adapt to evolving technologies, and leverage AI tools to work smarter and push your engineering capabilities further.

 - Travel to customer sites approximately 50% of the time.



About You

You are autonomous and high-agency, and you do whatever it takes to get the job done. You identify and define problems well in ambiguous situations, solve them effectively and efficiently, and stay relentless on the customer floor. You understand that a working first version delivered fast is worth more than a polished one delivered late.

You think from first principles and teach yourself new engineering skills without hand-holding. You use AI tools and seek subject matter experts to extend your engineering. You think in software, hardware, and process, and you weigh speed against engineering quality with good judgment. You know what an MVP looks like at a customer site. You communicate clearly with operators, executives, and engineers, and you can break work into near-term engineering steps while holding a longer-term strategy.

No specific degree or years of experience are required. Show us what you have built, fixed, or taught yourself, especially in messy real-world conditions.



Export Control Requirements

In order to comply with the export regulations of the United States Government, it is required that the applicant must fall under one of the following categories: (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (i.e. current green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.



Minimum Qualifications

We recognize that strong technical foundations can be developed through many different paths. Whether you're early in your career, bring years of hands-on experience, or have built your expertise through self-directed learning and independent exploration, we're interested in how you've developed your knowledge, strengthened your skills, and demonstrated your ability to apply these fundamentals.

 - Core engineering fundamentals: coordinate frames and transforms, forward and inverse kinematics, and how a sensor is positioned and calibrated within a robot's working environment.

 - Hands-on comfort with an off-the-shelf robot controller: setting one up, running it, and debugging it when it misbehaves.

 - Electrical and mechatronics competence in a hands-on setting: reading and debugging circuits, working with PLCs and microcontrollers, and understanding machine safety practice around industrial equipment.

 - Excellent prompt engineering - sufficient to prototype an idea, analyze data and build a feature.

 - The ability to take an ambiguous problem and break it into a system architecture and a plan, including choosing between candidate approaches on technical merit.

 - Clear communication with operators, engineers and executives, often on the same day and about the same problem.

 - Willingness to travel to customer sites approximately 50 percent of the time.

 - Must meet export control requirements in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization beginning at the time of hire through the entirety of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Hands-on work with robot arms, including integrating a motion interface such as ROS-Industrial, MoveIt or a vendor motion API.

 - Practical experience with vision sensors that you set up, calibrated and tuned yourself, on anything from an inexpensive off-the-shelf camera to a production vision system.

 - Experience with a robotics middleware or networking framework such as ROS, together with the network layer underneath it: moving data between robot controllers, sensors and higher-level software, working with industrial communication protocols, and bringing a distributed set of devices up and talking to each other on one network.

 - Work in a physics or robotics simulator, for example Isaac or Omniverse, Gazebo, RViz or MATLAB.

 - Familiarity with path planning and motion planning algorithms and the tradeoffs between them.

 - Demonstrated judgment in selecting the right algorithmic approach for a cyber-physical system or Physical AI implementation

 - Building your own data collection tooling while prototyping, and experience assembling datasets or training models for physical systems.

 - Use of AI-assisted engineering tools to move faster on design, analysis or implementation.

 - Working knowledge of manufacturing processes and how process parameters change the outcome on a real part. Experience in surface finishing manufacturing processes such as sanding, grinding, blasting or coating. Engineering mechanics and materials fundamentals, including how force, contact and abrasive media physically change a surface.

 - Measurement and documentation discipline: using standard metrology tools, and recording process data rigorously, including the visual and physical evidence that does not come out of a log file.

 - CAD and 3D modeling, including producing and reading manufacturing drawings.

 - Customer-facing deployment or commissioning experience in a live production environment.



GrayMatter Robotics provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We encourage and embrace applicants of all backgrounds to apply!



GrayMatter Robotics is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you believe you require accommodations during the recruiting process, please contact accommodations@graymatter-robotics.com to submit your request.



Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.



Depending on the position and if listed, compensation may include the base salary range, and equity. We also provide comprehensive benefits and perks which include but are not limited to medical, dental, vision, Flexible Time Off (FTO), 401(k) plan + employer match, regular offsite events, a discretionary fund for enhancing productivity and so much more! The range listed on job postings reflect the minimum and maximum new hire salary across levels in Los Angeles, CA.
